rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan parses the interrogative clause as the second object of أرأيتم understood as أخبروني; its answer is supplied by the preceding clause, yielding a question about what is permissible if Shuaib has clear proof.
rows.anchor: على ما قال أبو حيان في مثل هذا الكلام أعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib says he does not forbid their fraud and then secretly commit it himself by taking for himself what they have abandoned.
rows.anchor: وما أريد ( بنهيي إياكم عما أنهاكم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, خالفني إلى something means he pursued it while I turned away; خالفني عنه reverses the direction, with the speaker pursuing while the other turns away.
rows.anchor: خالفني فلان إلى كذا إذا قصده وأنت مول عنه وخالفني عنه

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr takes أن أخالفكم as the object of أريد, treats خالف as خلف, and reads إلى as attached to أخالف or to an implied مائلا; the sense is that Shuaib will not take their place in doing the forbidden act.
rows.anchor: قال في البحر : والظاهر ما ذكروه أن ( أن أخالفكم ) في موضع المفعول به لأريد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative supplies a coordinated omitted verb, وأميل, before the phrase about turning toward what Shuaib forbids.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في الكلام فعل محذوف معطوف على المذكور أي وأميل إلى إلخ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parsing keeps أخالف in its ordinary sense of opposing: the أن-clause is the object of أريد and إلى attaches to an implied مائلا, or the clause gives the purpose of أريد.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يبقى أخالف على ظاهره من المخالفة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the phrase as saying that Shuaib does not intend, by opposing them, to commit what he forbids them.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج في معنى ذلك : أي ما أقصد بخلافكم إلى ارتكاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib means that everything he says aims only to reform his people through counsel and exhortation, for as long as he is able and without sparing effort.
rows.anchor: بالنصيحة والموعظة ما استطعت أي مدة استطاعتي ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī prefers taking ما as a temporal verbal noun: Shuaib seeks reform throughout the period he remains able to do so.
rows.anchor: فما مصدرية ظرفية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parse makes ما a relative pronoun in apposition to الإصلاح, meaning the amount of reform Shuaib can manage; the apposition may be partitive, complete, or inclusive, with an understood pronoun where required.
rows.anchor: وجوز فيها أن تكون موصولة بدلا من الإصلاح أي المقدار الذي إستطعته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further parse treats ما استطعت as the direct object of the verbal noun الإصلاح, meaning the corrupt condition of the people that Shuaib can repair.
rows.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن تكون مفعولا به للمصدر المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī finds the preferred temporal reading stronger: the alternatives add ellipsis and lose emphasis; making the definite verbal noun govern an object is disallowed by Kufans and rare for Basrans, and also leaves an object of استطعت implicit.
rows.anchor: الأبلغ الأظهر ما قدمناه لأن في احتمال البدلية إضمار وفوات المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib's success in achieving the reform he seeks comes only through God's support and help.
rows.anchor: أي ما كوني موفقا لتحقيق ما أتوخاه من إصلاحكم إلا بالله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret Shuaib's success as guidance to truth and right judgment in everything he does or leaves undone, granted only by God.
rows.anchor: واختار بعضهم أن يكون المراد وما توفيقي لإصابة الحق والصواب في كل ما آتي وأذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense covers every individual instance of Shuaib's success, since an annexed verbal noun can be generic; alternatively, the whole genus is exclusive, entailing every instance by implication rather than explicitly.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد وما كل فرد من أفراد توفيقي لما صرحوا به من أن المصدر المضاف من صيغ العموم

rows.speaker: كثير
rows.claim: Many grammarians supply an omitted genitive after the preposition, yielding the idiomatic sense من عند الله; this avoids linking an agent's action to باء, which grammarians find inelegant because it marks an instrument.
rows.anchor: وتقدير المضاف بعد الباء مما التزمه كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied genitive can also clarify that human action is enabled by God's indication and help: indication alone does not produce success without divine aid.
rows.anchor: ومجرد الدلالة لا يجدي بدون المعونة منه عز شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib relies on God in this matter or all his affairs, since God alone has power while all else is inherently helpless and without standing.
rows.anchor: في ذلك أو في جميع أموري لا على غيره فإنه سبحانه القادر المتمكن من كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib returns to God in the matter at hand and directs all his concerns to Him rather than anyone else.
rows.anchor: أي أرجع فيما أنا بصدده أو أقبل بشراشري في مجامع أموري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is coordinated with what precedes; its present tense, like توكلت, evokes the scene and indicates continuing action despite a past form being more natural for settled realization.
rows.anchor: والجملة معطوفة على ما قبلها وكأن إيثار صيغة الاستقبال فيها على الماضي

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī reads Shuaib's three replies as honoring God's right through gratitude and service, the self's right by restraint, and people's right through reform and guidance.
rows.anchor: وفي أنوار التنزيل لأجوبته عليه السلام الثلاثة يعني

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī explains the lack of conjunction before إن أريد as confirmation of the preceding answer: someone seeking to take what he forbids for himself would not truly intend reform.
rows.anchor: بما نهى عنه لم يكن مريدا للإصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal to God's granting success removes any suggestion that Shuaib's mention of ability means he acts independently or arrogantly.
rows.anchor: إزاحة لما عسى أن يوهمه إسناد الاستطاعة إليه بإرادته من استبداده بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage points to pure monotheism, as does the pairing of worship and seeking help in the opening of al-Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: وفيه مع ما بعده إشارة إلى محض التوحيد

rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: Several commentators praise Shuaib's gentle, tactful argument, his effort to win assent and establish truth through seeking divine aid, and his show of having no fear of the unbelievers' hostility.
rows.anchor: مراعاة لطف المراجعة ورفق الاستنزال والمحافظة على حسن المجاراة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take Shuaib's return to God as an indirect threat of punishment; the author notes that voluntary turning to God in life is not the same as the compelled return for judgment.
rows.anchor: قيل : وفيه أيضا تهديدهم بالرجوع إلى الله تعالى للجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author questions the threat reading: in context الإنابة is voluntary turning to God, whereas the return that entails judgment is involuntary.
rows.anchor: أن الإنابة إنما هي الرجوع الاختياري بالفعل إليه سبحانه لا الرجوع الاضطراري للجزاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another possible threat is implicit in Shuaib's trust in God, who protects those relying on Him; the text says this need not mean a threat of punishment on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: لكن لا يتعين أن يكون ذلك تهديدا بالجزاء يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone has true supplication: it is rightly directed to Him, answered when made, and the genitive marks its exclusive relation to truth and its freedom from falsehood, error, and waste.
rows.anchor: أي الدعاء والتضرع الثابت الواقع في محله المجاب عند وقوعه

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī interprets this as supplication in fear, when people call only on God, and considers that reading closer to the verse's context; it is supported by the verse about those lost when people call on anyone but Him.
rows.anchor: وزعم الماوردي أن هذا أشبه بسياق الآية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reading takes دعوة as الدعاء, a request for response, and understands it as worship by inclusion; the genitive may be analyzed as attaching a described noun to its quality, so only God deserves worship.
rows.anchor: بمعنى الدعاء أي طلب الاقبال والمراد به العبادة للاشتمال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some supply an omitted complement, الدعاء للعبادة: God alone rightly summons people to worship Him, and this is inseparable from the claim that worship belongs to Him alone.
rows.anchor: إن الدعوة بمعنى الدعاء ومتعلقها محذوف أي للعبادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes الحق as God Himself: He is the true deity who hears the supplicant and answers.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أن المراد من الحق هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشف
rows.claim: The two principal readings serve the same polemic against associating rivals: whether الحق means truth opposed to falsehood or God's name, the construction marks His exclusive claim to supplication and worship.
rows.anchor: وبين صاحب الكشف حاصل الوجهين بأن الكلام مسوق لاختصاصه سبحانه بأن يدعى ويعبد

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشف
rows.claim: On the divine-name reading, replacing a pronoun with الظاهر الحق reinforces the lām and genitive, while God's true existence makes all else contingent on Him; alleged deities are false and cannot answer.
rows.anchor: ثم زيد ذلك باقامة الظاهر مقام المضمر معادا بوصف ينبىء عن اختصاصها به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The al-Kashf account answers Abū Ḥayyān's objection that the divine-name reading collapses into the awkward phrase الله دعوة الله, and makes al-Ṭībī's alternative gloss unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وبهذا سقط ما قاله أبو حيان في الاعتراض على الوجه الثاني

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: If the occasion was the story of Arbad and ʿĀmir, the preceding description of God as severe in stratagem connects to their unseen destruction and the Prophet's answered prayer; otherwise it warns disputing unbelievers of divine punishment, an answered prayer against them, or their error in worshipping others.
rows.anchor: وجه تعلق هذه والجملة التي قبلها أعني

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report about the Arbad and ʿĀmir episode says the Prophet prayed, “O God, restrain them from me as You will”; the author gives no grading.
rows.anchor: رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقد روى أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The same contextual argument could apply if the occasion of revelation was the story of a Jew or a tyrant.
rows.anchor: إن سبب النزول قصة اليهودي أو الجبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative phrase can refer to the idols that polytheists call upon; alternatively it refers to the polytheists, with the idols omitted as the object of يدعون because من دونه indicates worship beyond God.
rows.anchor: أي الأصنام الذين يدعونهم أي المشركون وحذف عائد الموصول في مثل ذلك كثير

rows.speaker: البزدوي
rows.claim: Al-Bazdawī's reading through Abū ʿAmr has the second-person تاء, تدعون, supporting the view that the relative phrase denotes the idols addressed by the polytheists.
rows.anchor: قراءة البزدوي عن أبي عمرو ( تدعون ) بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in لا يستجيبون refers to the relative under the first parsing and to its omitted object under the second; on either account the idols fail to answer the polytheists' requests.
rows.anchor: عليه عائد على ( الذين ) وعلى الثاني عائد على مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols give no response, just as water cannot move toward a person who stretches out his hands from afar and calls for it to reach his mouth without a vessel.
rows.anchor: إلا استجابة كاستجابة الماء لمن بسط كفيه إليه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān allows هو to refer to the mouth and the suffix in بالغه to water: in that posture the mouth cannot reach water, just as water cannot reach the mouth.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو حيان كون ( هو ) ضمير الفم والهاء في ( بالغه ) ضمير الماء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another parsing makes هو refer to the person extending his hands and the suffix in بالغه refer to water.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم كون الأول ضمير ( باسط ) والثاني ضمير الماء

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects making هو refer to باسط and the suffix to the mouth: a participle predicated of someone other than its subject must expose its subject, requiring the wording وما هو ببالغه الماء.
rows.anchor: اسم الفاعل إذا جرى على غير من هو له لزم إبراز الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual reading depicts utter failure precisely when the supplicant most needs an answer; the composite simile portrays urgent seekers before insensible, powerless idols and is framed as mockery.
rows.anchor: والغرض كما قال بعض المدققين ففي الاستجابة على البت بتصوير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is an absolute exception from the broadest verbal category; استجابة is apparently an active verbal noun, as required by the overt verb, though it may be passive and annexed to باسط by the active/passive verbal-noun relation.
rows.anchor: فالاستثناء مفرغ من أعم عام المصدر كما أشرنا إليه والظاهر أن الاستجابة هناك مصدر من المبني للفاعل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: If hands are spread to drink rather than gesture or call, the comparison is to a person trying to take water with open fingers and gaining nothing.
rows.anchor: وقد يراد من بسط الكفين إلى الماء بسطهما أي نشر أصابيعهما

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some describe the likeness as the meagerness of the result, though Al-Alūsī says it amounts to none; this is an individual simile of a futile effort, like writing on water, not a compound intellectual comparison.
rows.anchor: وجعل بعضهم وجه الشبه قلة الجدوى ولعله أراد عدمها

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from ʿAlī compares the image to a thirsty person at a well's brink without a rope, unable to reach the bottom while the water cannot rise to him; Al-Alūsī says this returns to the first interpretation.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أن ذلك تشبيه بعطشان على شفير بئر بلا رشاء

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda compares the futile appeal to clutching water, and says Arabs use the image for pursuing what cannot be attained; he cites two anonymous poems about grasping water by hand.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عبيدة أن ذلك تشبيه بالقابض على الماء

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An anonymous poem likens a lost bond of affection to someone holding water in his hand, witnessing the idiom's futility.
rows.anchor: فأصبحت فيما كان بيني وبينها من الود مثل القابض الماء باليد

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A second anonymous poem compares yearning for absent people to holding water that one's fingers cannot contain, illustrating the same futile pursuit.
rows.anchor: وإني وإياكم وشوقا إليكم كقابض ماء لم تسعه أنامله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī says the water-clutching proverb is closer to the open-finger drinking interpretation, but باسط itself means spreading fingers, not clasping; a poem about a hand unable to close supports that distinction.
rows.anchor: فان بسط الكف ظاهر في نشر الاصابيع ممدودة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The anonymous line تعود بسط الكف uses basting the palm for an open hand that cannot close, supporting the ordinary sense of باسط as fingers spread outward.
rows.anchor: تعود بسط الكف حتى لو أنه أراد انقباضا لم تطعه أنامله

rows.speaker: بكير بن معروف
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī rejects as unreliable a report attributed to Bukayr ibn Maʿrūf that باسط means Cain, punished after killing his brother by being held over the sea just beyond reach of the water.
rows.anchor: عن بكير بن معروف من أنه قابيل

rows.speaker: قراء
rows.claim: A variant reads كباسطٍ كفيه with tanwīn, meaning like any person who spreads his two hands.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( كباسط كفيه ) بالتنوين أي كشخص يبسط كفيه

words: وَمَا دُعَآءُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers' prayer is wasted, lost, and false; if it means prayer to idols, the claim follows from the previous verse and is repeated for emphasis.
rows.anchor: أي في ضياع وخسار وباطل والمراد بهذا الدعاء إن كان دعاء آلهتهم فظاهر

words: وَمَا دُعَآءُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: If the phrase means unbelievers' prayers to God, Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to say their voices are veiled from God so He does not hear them; Al-Alūsī limits this explanation to requests concerning the afterlife because some unbelievers' prayers, including Iblīs's, may be answered.
rows.anchor: من أن أصوات الكفار محجوبة عن الله تعالى فلا يسمع دعاؤهم

words: وَمَا دُعَآءُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view allows the phrase to mean their prayers to God without restricting it to unanswered requests, despite the objection that some such prayers are granted.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن يراد دعاؤهم مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī takes سجود as humility and submission: all creation is subject to God's decrees alone. Fronting لله gives exclusivity, ruling out any independent or shared submission to another.
rows.anchor: يخضع وينقاد لا لشيء غيره سبحانه استقلالا ولا اشتراكا فالقصر ينتظم القلب والإفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the apparent reading, من denotes angels and the two rational kinds, humans and jinn; they are singled out as central, and their submission demonstrates that of other beings. Alternatively it includes nonrational creation too, with من used by predominance.
rows.anchor: من الملائكة والثقلين كما يقتضيه ظاهر التعبير بمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusatives may be circumstantial adverbs; if a verbal noun cannot directly function as a state, understand them as طائعين وكارهين.
rows.anchor: نصب على الحال فان قلنا بوقوع المصدر حالا من غير تأويل فهو ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All submit to God's greatness and to the coming of His decrees of creation and annihilation, willingly or unwillingly, without another authority intervening in any of it.
rows.anchor: من غير مداخلة حكم غيره جل وعلا بل غير حكمه تعالى في شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parse makes the words causal accusatives; كره then means compulsion, a passive verbal noun so its agent matches the subject of prostration, while grammarians who do not require matching can retain its ordinary sense.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون النصب على العلة فالكره بمعنى الإكراه وهو مصدر المبني للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī answers that unwillingness can still be a cause: a cause is whatever prompts an act or results from it, not only an intended goal; the accusatives may alternatively be objects of absolute verbal force, سجود طوع وكره.
rows.anchor: وما قيل عليه من أن اعتبار العلية في الكره غير ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their shadows may mean those belonging to earthly beings alone, or to them and every dense body; al-Shihāb's marginal note advises referring the pronoun to earth-dwellers, since heavenly beings have no shadow absent metonymy or an inclusive reading.
rows.anchor: وفي الحواشي الشهابية ينبغي أن يرجع الضمير لمن في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shadow's submission consists in following God's will as He extends and contracts it, makes it recede, or causes it to disappear.
rows.anchor: ومعنى انقياد الظلال له تعالى أنها تابعة لتصرفه سبحانه ومشيئته في الامتداد والتقلص

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says ẓill was originally a verbal noun and then came to denote the image cast by a body, whether reversed or upright; further implications are discussed elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وأصل الظل كما قال الفراء مصدر ثم أطلق على الخيال الذي يظهر للجرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is temporal for an implicit سجود, with باء meaning في; morning and evening stand for continuous submission. If it modifies the shadows, their movement is especially visible at those times.
rows.anchor: ظرف للسجود المقدر والباء بمعنى في وهو كثير والمراد بهما الدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuduww is the plural of ghadāh; āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, the interval between afternoon and sunset, though it is also analyzed as a plural of aṣl from aṣīl with its second hamza changed to alif.
rows.anchor: والآصال جمع أصيل وهو مابين العصر والمغرب

rows.speaker: ابن مجلز
rows.claim: Ibn Mujliz reads الإيصال with kasra on the hamza, treating it as the verbal noun of آصلنا, “we entered the evening,” as Ibn Jinnī explains.
rows.anchor: بقراءة ابن مجلز ( الإيصال ) بكسر الهمزة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take prostration literally: unbelievers single out God in worship when forced by distress, as in the verse about people at sea calling on Him with sincere devotion.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن المراد حقيقة السجود فإن الكفرة حالة الاضطرار

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī suggests God may create understanding in shadows so they prostrate, as He did in mountains so they glorified Him and showed effects of divine manifestation.
rows.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يخلق الله تعالى في الظلال إفهاما وعقولا بها تسجد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the shadows' prostration as the visible posture of their owners; this requires a broad metaphor, an implied causative, or a defense that incidental metaphor or combining literal and figurative senses is permissible, with some options problematic.
rows.anchor: عموم المجاز في السجود المذكور في الآية بأن يراد به الوقوع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reads سجود as the bodily posture: angels and believers prostrate willingly, while those brought into Islam under the sword do so unwillingly, whether hypocritically or because compulsion marked their first state.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة أن السجود عبارة عن الهيئة المخصوصة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view calls willing those for whom prostration is easy and unwilling those who find it burdensome.
rows.anchor: كرها من يثقل عليه ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Since some beings do not prostrate, one view makes من general in wording but restricted in intended scope; another includes every rational being and takes يسجد as “must prostrate,” emphatically expressing obligation as occurrence.
rows.anchor: والمراد بيسجد يجب أن يسجد لكن عبر عن الوجوب بالوقوع مبالغة

rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī favors the cosmic-submission reading: the whole world, including shadows, is governed by God's will, so the beings worshipped by polytheists can neither harm nor benefit anyone.
rows.anchor: واختار غير واحد في تفسير الآية

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād argues that an idolater's prostration to God only in distress cannot establish the verse's exclusivity, since the same person worships idols in ease; universal submission through creation and annihilation is a stronger rebuke.
rows.anchor: وفي إرشاد العقل السليم بعد نقل ما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī rejects Ibn al-Anbārī's analogy: a mountain could have intellect if granted life, but a shadow is an accident incapable of life; its prostration is its shifting between sides and changing as God wills.
rows.anchor: الجبل يمكن أن يكون له عقل بشرط تقدير الحياة وأما الظل فعرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī first explains “from the sky” as from its direction, as observation suggests; others take it as from the sky itself and cite reports whose authenticity he leaves to God.
rows.anchor: أي من جهتها على ماهو المشاهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation regards the water as coming from the sky itself, with من used figuratively because heavenly bodies cause vapor to rise; ماء may mean much water or rain as a kind.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أنزل منها نفسها ( ماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain sends water through valleys where it falls, not through every valley since rain does not cover every region; أودية is the plural of واد.
rows.anchor: الامطار لاتستوعب الاقطار وهو جمع واد

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī says فاعل is not normally known to take an أفعلة plural; analogical overlap between فاعل and فعيل explains وادٍ/أودية, alongside the regular patterns أصحاب and أجربة and reciprocal examples أيتام and أشراف. The source notes a contrary example in Sharḥ al-Tashīl.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي : ولا يعلم أن فاعلا جمع على أفعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wādī can mean the channel through which much water flows, the cleft between mountains, or the flowing water itself; for the first sense the predication is figurative or has an omitted مياه, while the water sense makes it literal by naming the container for its contents.
rows.anchor: والوادي الموضع الذي يسيل فيه الماء بكثرة وبه سميت الفرجة بين الجبلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valley image is preferred to continuously flowing rivers because the valleys' changing capacity makes the likeness to the coming example clearer.
rows.anchor: لوضوح المماثلة بين شأنها وما مثل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بقدرها may mean the amount God fixed in wisdom for people's benefit, or an amount varying with the size and catchment of each valley; it need not fill each valley to its rim.
rows.anchor: بمقدارها الذي عينه الله تعالى واقتضته حكمته سبحانه في نفع الناس

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: If أودية means physical valleys, the phrase can mean that their waters flow in proportion to their capacity; its suffix may also refer by shifted usage to their waters.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى سالت مياهها بقدر تلك الأودية

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī attaches بقدرها to سالت; Abū al-Baqāʾ makes it an adjective of أودية, and another parsing attaches it to أنزل.
rows.anchor: عن الحوفي متعلق بسالت وقال أبو البقاء : إنه في موضع

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī, and one narration from Abū ʿAmr read بقدرها with a silent دال, a dialectal variant.
rows.anchor: الأشهب العقيلي وأبو عمرو في رواية ( بقدرها ) بسكون الدال
